AGent Energy, a Houston-based startup that integrates backup generators into the grid during emergencies, raised $11 million in seed funding co-led by Spero Ventures and MassMutual Ventures. Intrepid Investment Management and existing investors CIV and Zero Infinity Partners joined the round, which ranks among the largest seed rounds ever for a US transportation and energy startup — above the 97th percentile. hits.snippet: ## AGent Energy Raises $11 Million Series Seed Round AGent Energy, an AI-driven distributed power plant developer in the behind-the-meter renewable energy market, has closed an $11 million Series Seed financing round co-led by Spero Ventures and MassMutual Ventures. The round brings the company’s total funding to $17 million within 12 months of its founding. Intrepid Investment Management joined the round as a new investor, alongside existing backers CIV and Zero Infinity Partners (ZIP), which had provided AGent Energy’s earlier funding. ## Investors Back AGent Energy’s Growth “Closing $17 million in our first year reflects both the urgency of the grid reliability challenge and the speed at which our team executes,” said Stephanie Hendricks, CEO and co-founder of AGent Energy. [...] Skip to content . AGent Energy’s AI-based platform aggregates and dispatches distributed generation at commercial, industrial, and institutional sites, targeting more than 200 gigawatts of behind-the-meter capacity.
